I've always wondered if there was a Lego SCP, and this… is brilliant.

every company interviewed by undercover Agents thus far has denied ever making irregular Lego.

Oh yeah, and the last addendum… it's slightly disturbing, but mostly hilarious. No one likes rip-off Lego.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I actually think the article means they are Lego brand construction blocks (Something backed up by the Megablocks crosstest).

The article says:

It has no brand name, and every company interviewed by undercover Agents thus far has denied ever making irregular Lego.

Which is inconsistent with the idea that these are LEGO bricks. If they are LEGOs they would be branded, and the only company to speak with would be the LEGO Group.

Might be worth correcting that and the minifig thing.

I think altering the quoted sentence so that it no longer refers to unbranded blocks and multiple companies is definitely a content change and doesn't qualify as an allowed edit. Changing "Legoman" to "Minifig" is more borderline, but I wouldn't do it without moderator approval first.

Fair use out of universe, and makes sense in-universe as a specific detail- similar to mentioning a specific model of car or something, to establish that it's not a mass-produced anomaly, but something about this particular item.

I am of the opinion that proper clinical tone means no slang, and that using trademarks generically (unless they are wholly genericized and a court has since ruled them longer legally binding; as with "aspirin' in 1921 — this is absolutely not the case here where the LEGO Group has historically defended the trademark quite aggressively) is a form of slang. I know that others have disagreed with me in the past on this issue, but I still believe that I am correct.
